note: Forested area on the upper Castor River with the granite Castor River Shut-Ins; the primitive camping area sits at the end of a gravel road above Combs Branch, reached from County Road 248 on the south side rather than the shut-ins road. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: one MDC-designated primitive camping area at the end of the MDC improved gravel road from CR 248 (no ford on that road), free, FCFS, no hookups. Pin on the camping point, 66 m from the lot. Not waterfront confirmed. Directions on file point to the shut-ins side, not the camping.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: the area page lists 'Designated Camping Sites'; the 2024 area map shows one Primitive Camping symbol with a parking lot at the north end of the MDC Improved Road that runs ~3 km north from County Road 248 along ridges (no stream crossing on it). Imagery shows a gravel road ending in a short gravel pull-out (~34 x 8 m) at the edge of a field; MDC GIS camping point 37.54485,-90.15163, lot 37.54479,-90.15088 (66 m). A 23-ft rig reaches it on gravel; no posted limit. The map's 'Deep Ford' symbols sit on County Road 208 by the shut-ins (north side) - the route in the stored directions ('Route W south, then County Road 208 east') - not on the road to the camping, so the note now says the camping is reached from CR 248.
WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront): confirmed. Combs Branch is ~200 m north across a field; the Castor River is ~1.5 km west.
Pin is the MDC camping point - fine.
Note rewritten: the stored directions led to the shut-ins via a road with fords; replaced with where the camping actually is.
